{!{$controller_gameplay_move|5}} - move
   (with {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}} held) move targeting reticule
{!{$controller_gameplay_action|5}} - pickup item or activate stairs/lever,
   (with {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}} held) use item from ground
   (with {!LStick} direction) action (open/close door)
{!{$controller_gameplay_fire|5}} - Fire
   (with {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}} held) alternative fire (if present)
{!{$controller_gameplay_reload|5}} - Reload
   (with {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}} held) alternative/dual reload (if present)
{!{$controller_gameplay_player|5}} - open inventory (use {!Left}/{!Right} or shoulders
   to change panels), with {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}} held - open equipment
{!{$controller_gameplay_menu|5}} - game menu
{!{$controller_gameplay_target_prev|5}} - previous target
{!{$controller_gameplay_target_next|5}} - next target
{!{$controller_gameplay_active|5}} - (press) use active class skill (i.e. {!Adrenaline})
{!{$controller_gameplay_swap|5}} - (press) swap weapon with prepared weapon
   (with {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}}) held - unload weapon from ground or inventory
{!{$controller_gameplay_up},{$controller_gameplay_down},{$controller_gameplay_left},{$controller_gameplay_right}} - move targeting reticule
             (might be removed in the future)
{!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_run|5}} -- hold to show quickslots,
   {!{$controller_gameplay_up},{$controller_gameplay_down},{$controller_gameplay_left},{$controller_gameplay_right}} direction to use

help.body.gamepad.alternate-modifier:
Holding {!{$controller_gameplay_modifier_alt}} will enable alternative actions as below
and add hint info on the targeted square.
help.body.gamepad.continuous-movement:
After a move you can hold the {!{$controller_gameplay_move}} button and change direction with the
{!Left Stick} to do multiple moves - this works if there are no enemies
in sight, you will automatically stop if an enemy appears. You will also
not automatically move into hazardous terrain, such as lava or acid.
help.body.gamepad.equipment-controls:
{!RShoulder}/{!LShoulder} - change panels.
{!Y} - drop ( with {!RTrigger} drop and unload weapon)
{!X} - swap item in Equipment
{!LTrigger+DPad} - assign quickslot to direction
help.body.gamepad.movement:
Movement is done by moving the {!Left Stick} to the desired direction and
confirming it with the {!{$controller_gameplay_move}} button.
help.body.gamepad.title: {rController}
help.body.gamepad.ui-controls:
{!A} - confirm, {!B} - cancel, {!D-Pad} selection, also {!RShoulder} and
{!LShoulder} to change panels.
help.body.intro.accessible-design:
Unlike many other roguelikes, DRL is intended to be simple and easy to
get into. To that end, there is a limited inventory, maps of the size of
one screen, and one item per tile. The number of keys you need to 
remember is also quite small compared to many other games in its genre.
help.body.intro.mission:
Your quest in DRL is to descend into the moonbase complex, find the
source of this evil outbreak, and destroy it at all costs.
help.body.intro.premise:
DRL is inspired by a famous 1993 FPS hellish shooter. You're
the sole surviving marine from a squad sent to investigate a distress call
from the moonbase of Phobos.  It turns out that all hell has broken loose
on the plant... literally.
help.body.intro.roguelike:
{rDRL} (abbr. for D, the Roguelike) is, as the name implies, a
roguelike game. If you don't know what a roguelike is... checkout 
wikipedia -- {Bhttp://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roguelike}.
help.body.intro.title: {rIntroduction}
help.body.keys.binding-notice:
Most keybindings can be redefined via the file Settings menu. The 
  following set describes the standard layout, and does not reflect
  any changes you may have made to your keybindings.
help.body.keys.equipment-default:
Selecting a worn item will unequip it. Selecting an empty slot will
  let you choose an item. Note though, that switching through the
  inventory screen is faster.

{!Backspace} -- drop selected item
  {!Tab}       -- swap item with item in inventory

help.body.start.advanced-master-traits:
You'll notice a few traits aren't available. Some are "Advanced Traits",
and require you to learn a normal trait first. Advanced Traits are more
situational but quite effective, too. The rest are master traits, which
require you to take a specific set of traits (and block off a few other
traits) and give you some sort of great unique bonus. But hey, don't think
about it too hard. Just pick one you like and move on.
help.body.start.armor-durability:
Hey, you think you're cool because you found some armor? Think again. Look,
there are three numbers by the armor. The first two in square brackets are
[current damage resistance/maximum damage resistance]. The second one is 
your armor's health. 100% means it's undamaged, 1% is almost destroyed.
The more damaged an armor is, the lower its actual resistance is. Keep an
eye on those numbers!
help.body.start.artifacts:
5) {YArtifacts} - Artifact items are similar to unique items, except that they
can only appear in very specific special levels, while never appearing
randomly. Finding and collecting these items is almost always a very
challenging task.
help.body.start.assemblies:
2) {CAssemblies} - These items can be assembled from other items, usually 
common, by modding them with a specific set of mods. Experiment, as
discovered (assembled) assemblies will be recorded in your player data and
can be accessed with the "A" key during the game.
help.body.start.character-name:
The third decision you have to make is what your name will be in the game.
You can figure that much on your own, right? You can also leave it blank
and wear the name of a random legendary warrior...
help.body.start.class:
The second decision is choosing a character class. Classes differ by 
starting perks, availability of one advanced trait as basic, and each of
them has a different set of Master Traits.
help.body.start.common-items:
1) {!Common} - These items are... "common"? You will see them all across the
game, and what you should rely on. Most are generated randomly, but you
will find some are guaranteed in certain places (as a reward for completing
a special level, for example). Common weapons and armor accept 1/1, 3/2,
and 5/3 mods, respectively, depending on the level of your Whizkid trait.
help.body.start.damage-resistance:
Additionally each armor may grant additional resistance to specific damage 
types. This information can be obtained in the inventory and equipment 
screens.
help.body.start.difficulty:
Before you start your game, you have to make a few decisions. The first is
the difficulty level. At the beginning, only three difficulty levels are
available: "I'm too young to die", "Hey, Not Too Rough", and "Hurt Me
Plenty". At higher difficulties, more monsters appear and tougher monsters
appear earlier. "Ultra-Violence" and "Nightmare!" difficulties are unlocked
as your player rank rises. At Nightmare! difficulty, only the most insane
DRL warriors will stand a chance!
help.body.start.dodging:
Getting hit too frequently when trying to approach an enemy (or when
running from him)? Try not to move in a straight line -- move diagonally,
as this increases your chance to dodge. If you don't want to approach or
retreat from the enemy, but also don't want to be hit often, try moving
from side-to-side, perpendicular to the direction of enemy, as this
gives you the same bonus as moving diagonally). Sometimes, in emergencies,
switching to the running tactic and using both of these tricks at once will
give you a much greater chance to dodge than normal.
help.body.start.equipment-status:
In the column to the right of that, you have two indicators, "Armor" and
"Weapon", that show you what armor and weapon you have equipped. For
weapons, the number in brackets indicates the damage that the weapon
deals, and the two numbers in square brackets indicate the current-loaded
ammo and clip size for that weapon (e.g., [4/6] means you have four
bullets in a magazine that can hold six).
help.body.start.exotic-items:
3) {VExotic} - These items are rarer and more powerful than common items.
They can potentially appear more than once per game, but are more often
than not found in special levels. Exotic weapons and armor can hold the
 same amounts of mods that their common counterparts do.
help.body.start.fire-targeting:
Oh, I almost forgot! To shoot, just press "f" to fire at the currently 
selected target! You can swap between visible targets using "TAB", or 
hold "Ctrl" to move the target reticule manually with the arrow keys.
Some weapons allow an alternative fire mode, such as the chainfiring 
mode of the chaingun - to use it, press "SHIFT-f".
help.body.start.first-floor:
This is a map of the first level of the moonbase on Phobos. The whole level
is exactly the size of the screen. Walk around (using the arrow keys or
numpad) and get used to the interface. Don't get yourself killed!
help.body.start.health-experience:
On the bottom you have the status bar. The top line displays your name, and
below it is the most important stat -- your health. If this one drops
below one percent, you're dead, dude - nothing can save you. Scanning 
to the right you can see the experience indicator. The first number is your
character level -- the higher it is, the tougher you are. The second number
is your experience displayed as a percentage. Each character level requires
a certain experience amount needed to achieve it.
help.body.start.inventory-equipment:
Press "i" to see your inventory. It's pretty empty, right? Your character
starts equipped with a few things -- your trusty pistol (already equipped),
a handful of ammo, and a couple of med-packs. To check equipped item,
press "e" in-game to see the full list (which includes boots and a second
weapon slot).
help.body.start.item-types: There are five types of items in this game:
help.body.start.levers-barrels:
Along the way, you're bound to run into levers ("&") and barrels ("0"). To
pull a lever, stand on it and press "SPACE" to use them. The effects are
random, so pull them at your own peril! And if you've ever played a shooter
you know what to expect with barrels: They all explode quite nicely, but
with varying effects depending on the barrel. (Be aware that levers are
activated with the same button as using items -- in this case, open up
your inventory and use the item from there by selecting it and pressing
ENTER.)
help.body.start.look-help:
Whenever you see something that you aren't familiar with, press "l" to
trigger the Look command -- moving the cursor with the arrow keys will
show what's under the cursor in the message bar. You can also press "h"
in-game to open up the help menu.
help.body.start.map-symbols:
Between the status bar and message bar, there's the map. The "@" sign with
the cursor below it -- that's you (aren't you ugly?). See any letters
nearby? It may be a "T"ree, but chances are it's the enemy. Kill'em all.
The "#" are walls, "+" is a closed door, "/" an open door. Dots are normal
floor. Red dots are either Phobos's ugly rock landscape (on the first
level), or blood (anywhere else).
help.body.start.menu-introduction:
When you first start a game of DRL, you're presented with a menu screen
with a few different options:
help.body.start.menu-options:
{YNew game} will, well, start a new game!
{YChallenge game} is initially locked, and becomes unlocked after you reach
Corporal rank (need to survive 10 levels for it). Challenge games force you
to play the game a certain way (e.g. using only melee), and you can raise
your player rank in DRL by completing them. As your rank goes higher, 
more challenges will be made available to you.
{YCustom game} brings up a selection screen where you can view and load
modules. Modules are player-created levels, episodes, or entirely new games
that bring a completely new experience to the DRL engine.
{YShow highscores} displays the highscore list, not surprisingly.
{YShow player} displays your player statistics, which include your player 
rank, number of kills, and number of wins. It has several screens which
can be scrolled with the arrow keys.
{YHelp} displays the help screen, which contains the info you are
currently reading.
help.body.start.message-area:
Take a look at the screen. It is divided into three parts. On top you have
the "message area", made of two lines of text. Watch this space carefully
-- it may notify you of impending danger or tell you that you're out of
ammo (poor sob!).
help.body.start.mod-packs:
Mods (Displayed by a " symbol) are little packs that enhance your weaponry
or armor. Most equipment you find can be modded, so try to cover up their
weaknesses by modding them.
help.body.start.pickup-consumables:
Your pistol and ammo are not going to last you very long, though.  Press
"g" to pick up new weapons (represented by "}") and ammo ("|").  If you
walk around that first level you're likely to run into some small medkits
(red "+") that you can pick up and add to your inventory. Later on you
might find other consumable items, they're all "+"s. Press "i" at any time
and a consumable to use it at any time. If you ever want to drop something
(usually to make room for new weapons or items), press "Backspace" in the
inventory screen to drop items.
help.body.start.player-information:
Try to check out player information screen by pressing "p" -- some useful
information is written there. First, there are your main parameters:
movement, firing, and reloading speeds, as well as your chance to hit with
the weapon you currently have equipped (from point blank range). Next are
the more passive statistics: your player and dungeon level, amount of
played turns, and your score so far. At the bottom you can find parameters
of equipment that you are currently wearing: damage, firing and reloading
speeds, and accuracy for weapons; and protection value, durability, and
movement and knockback modifiers for armor and boots (yes, armor and boots
can affect your movement speed and chance to be knocked back by powerful
attacks).
help.body.start.powerups:
As you go deeper into the base, you'll also find some power-ups ("^"). They
are used as soon as you pick them up, and several contain powerful effect,
so use them wisely.
help.body.start.prepared-weapon:
In the equipment menu (remember, press "e") you'll see that you have a
primary weapon equipped and a secondary weapon at hand.  By pressing "z"
you can switch your primary out for your secondary.  This is faster than
equipping a new weapon from your inventory and it saves you valuable
space.  It's also quite useful in a firefight, when the situation can
change at any moment!
help.body.start.reload-melee:
Ok, I hear you cry -- "Out of ammo!" Don't panic. Press "r" to reload your
weapon (Some weapons allow you an alternative reload by pressing SHIFT-r).
Reloading the correct ammo is automatic if you have it in your inventory.
But what if you don't? You can try pounding on the enemy with your fists
or a hand-to-hand weapon -- to do that just walk into him.  Pick up a
Berserk Pack or a chainsaw (or at least a knife) and you can do some
serious damage that way!
help.body.start.screen-introduction:
And that's it, you're ready to play the game! After a brief intro, you will
be greeted with something like this (ASCII map is present if playing in
ASCII mode):
help.body.start.start-first-game:
For now, select {YNew game} with the arrow keys and press ENTER to start
your very first game of DRL!
help.body.start.starting-trait:
The fourth and final choice to make is select a starting "trait". 
Traits are upgrades or "perks" that you earn when you gain levels in 
DRL (by killing monsters). Traits can raise your max health, let you
run faster, deal more damage per shot, or otherwise make you more awesome.
Some traits can be levelled up individually.
help.body.start.tactics:
Below your health and experience is "tactics". By default your tactic is
"cautious". This tactic gives no benefits or disadvantages. If you press
X once, it will change to "running" (note that changing tactics takes
some in-game time). With this tactic you have increased movement speed,
dodge chance, and defense bonus, but have a smaller chance to hit and
reduced melee damage. After some time spent running (or after pressing
X again), you will get "tired". Being tired has no effects, positive
or negative (like cautious), but while tired, you can't run again. You can
return to the cautious tactic by leveling up, gaining health by most
methods, or descending to next level. Since running is limited in this way,
try not to waste it. At the same time, however, remember to use it, as they
don't stockpile for later levels.
help.body.start.title: {rGetting Started}
help.body.start.unique-items:
4) {GUniques} - Unique items, as the name suggests, can only appear once per
game. Some of them just have cool stats, while others have special
abilities, and each of them come with a unique name. No unique item is
guaranteed, although they can appear in special levels, and they are quite
rare otherwise. Most uniques cannot be modded, but those that do can only
be modded if the player is playing the Technician class.

message.plot.apostle-victory:
The Apostle is dead.

You've beaten the forces of Hell, and yet, you've also managed to emerge victorious when reality changed to something else...  

You can rest easily...
At least until...

DRL II : Hell on Earth!
message.plot.carmack-sacrifice:
The thermonuclear bomb shows the last second, and you know that your life is over. Still as you look at the greatest of evils, your eyes meet, and you smile. To your surprise he smiles back, appearing satisfied.

The thermonuclear explosion erupts, and although you know that nothing can possibly survive, you also feel that this was a hollow victory. What could he have possibly been smiling for?  Perhaps you should have lived long enough to find out...
message.plot.carmack-victory:
John Carmack is dead.

No more evil will ever fall upon this world. Your damned soul rests, knowing that no more hellish forces will threaten Earth.

Or will they?

This will be revealed in...

DRL II : Hell on Earth!
message.plot.deimos-arrival:
Once you beat the big badasses and clean out the moon base you're supposed to win, aren't you? Aren't you? Where's your fat reward and ticket back home? What the hell is this? It's not supposed to end this way!

It stinks like rotten meat but it looks like the lost Deimos base. Looks like you're stuck on The Shores of Hell. And the only way out is through...
message.plot.earth-return:
The loathsome Spiderdemon that masterminded the invasion of the moon bases and caused so much death has had her ass kicked for all time.

A hidden doorway opens and you enter. You've proven too tough for Hell to contain, and now Hell at last plays fair -- for you emerge from the door to see the green fields of Earth! Home at last.

You wonder what's been happening on Earth while you were battling evil unleashed. It's good that no Hellspawn could have come through that door with you...

Or could it...?
message.plot.hell-arrival:
You've done it! The hideous Cyberdemon lord that ruled the lost Deimos moon base has been slain and you are triumphant!  But ... where are you? You clamber to the edge of the moon and look down to see the awful truth.

Deimos floats above Hell itself! You've never heard of anyone escaping from Hell, but you'll make the bastards sorry they ever heard of you! Quickly, you rappel down to the surface of Hell.

Now, it's on to the final chapter of DRL -- Inferno!
message.plot.intro-contact:
Suddenly...

"Hell, what a bloodbath!" you hear from the comm. "Corpses Everywhere!"

"What happened?!"

"Look, there's someone there!"

"Oh, no! God!"

Gunshots.

More Gunshots.
message.plot.intro-silence:
"This can't be happening!"

"Help! Help, I'm..." <SPLAT!>

"Jake! Where are you?! What happ... oh, fuck!"

<BANG! BANG! BANG!>

Slurp.

Silence.
message.plot.intro-wait:
The trip was long -- you thought it would never end. But hell, a marine's job is rarely interesting. You hate the UAC -- nothing ever happens here. Now you've got to sit around and wait for your squadmates, who are supposed to check out what happened on Phobos.

Not knowing what to do with yourself, you lean back near the comm console and listen for news from your fellow marines.
message.plot.sacrifice-mastermind:
The thermonuclear bomb shows the last second, and you know that your life is over. Still as you look at the Spider Mastermind, your eyes meet, and you smile. She is surprised, but after a split-second she understands.

The thermonuclear explosion erupts, and you laugh knowing that your sacrifice has ended the reign of Hell...

                             ...but did you get ALL of them?

term.being.agony.desc: Seems like the pain elementals' big momma!
term.being.agony.name: agony elemental
term.being.angel.desc: Why doesn't a BFG work when you really need it? As if from a half-forgotten nightmare, you encounter the harbinger of death...
term.being.angel.kill-desc-melee: was ripped apart by the Angel of Death
term.being.angel.name: Angel of Death
term.being.apostle.desc: This seems so unreal, as though from another story...
term.being.apostle.name: Apostle
term.being.arachno.desc: Evil can't get any purer. Spiderdemons equipped with a rapid-fire plasma cannon. Machine and flesh combined, kill on sight...
term.being.arachno.name: arachnotron
term.being.arch.desc: The worst thing you can encounter. With some unholy power far beyond your grasp they attack you with hellish flame, and can summon back the enemies you've worked so hard to banish!
term.being.arch.name: arch-vile
term.being.arenamaster.desc: The meanest, ugliest and strongest Arch-Vile you have ever seen...
term.being.arenamaster.kill-desc: was charred by the Arena Master
term.being.arenamaster.name: Arena Master
term.being.baron.desc: Huge, almost humanoid, acid ball hurling monsters from your worst nightmares. They are the nobility of Hell.
term.being.baron.kill-desc: was bruised by a baron of hell
term.being.baron.kill-desc-melee: was ripped open by a baron of hell
term.being.baron.name: baron of hell
term.being.bruiser.desc: Tough as a dump truck and nearly as big, these Goliaths are the worst things on two legs since Tyrannosaurus Rex.
term.being.bruiser.kill-desc: was baptised by a bruiser brother
term.being.bruiser.kill-desc-melee: was pounded rather hard by a bruiser brother
term.being.bruiser.name: bruiser brother
term.being.cacodemon.desc: Big flying red horned heads. They spit huge explosive plasma balls. If you don't have the weapon to handle them, better run...
term.being.cacodemon.kill-desc-melee: got too close to a cacodemon
term.being.cacodemon.name: cacodemon
term.being.captain.desc: Those were once really hardened marines, the tough fighting force of Earth. Now they're on the demonic side. They're really eager to make Swiss cheese out of you with their rapid fire chainguns...
term.being.captain.kill-desc: was perforated by a former captain
term.being.captain.kill-desc-melee: was maimed by a former captain
term.being.captain.name: former captain
term.being.commando.desc: These guys were evil to begin with. Being warped by Hell's power has only made them worse. Wielding a deadly plasma weapon, they should be treated with care... and lead.
term.being.commando.kill-desc: was melted by former commando's plasma gun
term.being.commando.kill-desc-melee: was killed by a former commando
term.being.commando.name: former commando
term.being.cyberdemon.desc: Monster and machine, combined. Equipped with a rocket launcher, this nightmare is the worst thing you can find in Hell. Or at least that is what you hope...
term.being.cyberdemon.kill-desc-melee: was ripped apart by a Cyberdemon
term.being.cyberdemon.name: Cyberdemon
term.being.demon.desc: You thought pink is cute? You won't anymore after meeting one of these bastards -- they are strong, tough and eager to rip your head off...
term.being.demon.name: demon
term.being.ecaptain.desc: These are the elite among the former captains. Beware of the superior firepower! Too bad their weapons are set to self-destruct on death.
term.being.ecaptain.kill-desc: was perforated by an elite captain
term.being.ecaptain.kill-desc-melee: was maimed by an elite captain
term.being.ecaptain.name: elite former captain
term.being.ecommando.desc: As expected, these ex-human soldiers are the best of the best! Armored, resilient and with superior firepower! Too bad their weapons are set to self-destruct on death.
term.being.ecommando.kill-desc: was melted by an elite commando's gun
term.being.ecommando.kill-desc-melee: was killed by an elite commando
term.being.ecommando.name: elite former commando
term.being.eformer.desc: These are the elite among the former humans. As stupid as their regular counterparts, but more resilient and packing quite a punch. Too bad their weapons are set to self-destruct on death.
term.being.eformer.kill-desc: was killed by an elite former human
term.being.eformer.kill-desc-melee: was killed by an elite former human
term.being.eformer.name: elite former human
term.being.esergeant.desc: These are the elite among the former sergeants. And they carry firepower to boot! Too bad their weapons are set to self-destruct on death.
term.being.esergeant.kill-desc: was shot by an elite sergeant
term.being.esergeant.kill-desc-melee: was maimed by an elite sergeant
term.being.esergeant.name: elite former sergeant
term.being.former.desc: Your fellow soldiers who went crazy because of the demonic influence. There's no hope for them anymore... only lead can heal their corrupted souls...
term.being.former.name: former human
term.being.imp.desc: Brown demonic servants from Hell, imps can throw fireballs at you. They're tough, mean and strong, and think only about sending you into oblivion...
term.being.imp.name: imp
term.being.jc.desc: You knew it. This is the true EVIL behind the invasion! This is the true mastermind of Hell! Kill him for he knows not the meaning of mercy! Kill him!! Kill him NOW!!!
term.being.jc.name: John Carmack
term.being.knight.desc: These are Hell's warlords. They command hellish armies to battle. Not as tough as Barons but are still a pain in the ass...
term.being.knight.kill-desc: was splayed by a hell knight
term.being.knight.kill-desc-melee: was gutted by a hell knight
term.being.knight.name: hell knight
term.being.lava-elemental.kill-desc: was burned by a lava elemental
term.being.lava-elemental.kill-desc-mele: was burned by a lava elemental
term.being.lava-elemental.name: lava elemental
term.being.lostsoul.desc: Quick flying fiery skull. These are the souls lost in Hell. Let them rest in peace, or rather, in pieces...
term.being.lostsoul.kill-desc-melee: was spooked by a lost soul
term.being.lostsoul.name: lost soul
term.being.mancubus.desc: It's big, it's mean, and it has two rocket launchers. What can be worse?
term.being.mancubus.name: mancubus
term.being.mastermind.desc: You guess the Arachnotrons had to come from somewhere. Hi, mom. She doesn't have a plasma gun, so thank heaven for small favors. Instead, she has a super-chaingun.
term.being.mastermind.kill-desc: let the Spider Mastermind pwn him
term.being.mastermind.name: Spider Mastermind
term.being.narachno.desc: Pure nightmare spiders. You'd wish they weren't there...
term.being.narachno.kill-desc: let an nightmare arachnotron get him
term.being.narachno.name: nightmare arachnotron
term.being.narch.desc: Oh God... *WHY* do they come in the nightmare variety too?
term.being.narch.name: nightmare arch-vile
term.being.ncacodemon.desc: Hell's latest improvement on demonic warfare - they're stronger, tougher, and angrier than ever.
term.being.ncacodemon.kill-desc: was fried by a nightmare cacodemon
term.being.ncacodemon.kill-desc-melee: was flattened by a nightmare cacodemon
term.being.ncacodemon.name: nightmare cacodemon
term.being.ndemon.desc: You liked it better when these guys were pink. Meet the stronger, tougher, more resilient way to meet your death.
term.being.ndemon.kill-desc-melee: was eaten alive by a nightmare demon
term.being.ndemon.name: nightmare demon
term.being.nimp.desc: Are you seeing things? What's with the color change? And why is it taking so much longer to kill these things!?
term.being.nimp.kill-desc: was burned by a nightmare imp
term.being.nimp.kill-desc-melee: was eviscerated by a nightmare imp
term.being.nimp.name: nightmare imp
term.being.nknight.desc: The nightmare side of the knight and baron strain. You hope it won't get worse than this. You hope...
term.being.nknight.kill-desc: was splayed by a nightmare knight
term.being.nknight.kill-desc-melee: was gutted by a nightmare knight
term.being.nknight.name: nightmare knight
term.being.nlostsoul.desc: The flying bluish skull. Wouldn't be a problem if there weren't so many of these nightmarish things...
term.being.nlostsoul.kill-desc-melee: was terrified by a nightmare soul
term.being.nlostsoul.name: nightmare soul
term.being.nmancubus.desc: What's blue and has two rocket launchers? Something worse.
term.being.nmancubus.kill-desc-melee: was flattened by a nightmare mancubus
term.being.nmancubus.name: nightmare mancubus
term.being.npain.desc: Pain, pain, pain, nightmare pain. Oh and nightmare souls...
term.being.npain.name: nightmare elemental
term.being.nrevenant.desc: This revenant has been dusted off and wired up one time too many. And it shows...
term.being.nrevenant.kill-desc: couldn't evade a nightmare revenant's fireball

term.trait.ammochain.desc: True gunners do not think of such unimportant things like ammo supply! As long as you use your trusty chain-fire weapons you only use up one ammo per volley!
term.trait.ammochain.name: Ammochain
term.trait.armydead.desc: You're the fucking army of justice. When you fire your trusty shotgun, no armor is a protection!
term.trait.armydead.name: Army of the Dead
term.trait.armydead.quote: "Might makes light! And I feel mighty!"
term.trait.badass.desc: You're the ultimate badass. Your blood runs so cold that it could make Hell freeze over (if they weren't too scared to take you). For each level, your maximum health before decay sets in is 50% higher, and you're knocked back one space less.
term.trait.badass.name: Badass
term.trait.badass.quote: "Who's the man? I'm the man! How bad? Real bad! I'm a 12.0 on a 10.0 scale of badness!"
term.trait.berserker.desc: You hate this place, you hate these stupid monsters, and you HATE that this is all happening to you. In fact you hate it so much that there's a chance that you'll fly into a berserk rage when you repeatedly smack someone in melee, or get hit hard enough. (NOTE: You do NOT get the healing effect of a Berserk Pack.)
term.trait.berserker.name: Berserker
term.trait.berserker.quote: "Who's a man and a half? I'm a man and a half! Berserker packin' man and a half!"
term.trait.bitch.desc: You're the meanest, toughest bastard in your entire squad. You relish pain and enjoy dishing it out even more. Even demons know you by name, because with every level of this trait, you do 1 more damage than your average Marine.
term.trait.bitch.name: Son of a bitch
term.trait.bitch.quote: "Kill them all, let God sort them out."
term.trait.blademaster.desc: You've mastered melee combat. Each time you finish off an opponent, you're immediately ready for another kill, and gain a free action!
term.trait.blademaster.name: Blademaster
term.trait.brute.desc: You don't need a gun - guns are for wusses! With each level of this trait you'll deal 3 more damage while bashing your enemies with your hands, knives, body parts, or whatever else is available. Also your melee accuracy increases by 2.
term.trait.brute.name: Brute
term.trait.brute.quote: "There's nothing wrong that I can't fix... with my hands!"
term.trait.bulletdance.desc: Pistols are your game -- you can squeeze an additional shot from each of your pistols for each level of Triggerhappy at half the time cost!
term.trait.bulletdance.name: Bullet Dance
term.trait.cateye.desc: Your eyes are so sharp they could cut through concrete. This trait lets you see your enemies from two spaces further away - and that means more time to shoot them!
term.trait.cateye.name: Cateye
term.trait.cateye.quote: "Huh? Whuzzat? Whuzzat? I like what I see!"
term.trait.dodgemaster.desc: The battlefield is a dance for you! Each first sidestep after your move will automatically succeed.
term.trait.dodgemaster.name: Dodgemaster
term.trait.dodgemaster.quote: "Knock, knock. Who's there? Me, me, me, me, ME!"
term.trait.dualgunner.desc: You're the kind of guy for whom one is never enough. When you and your buddies cruised bars Earthside, you always had a beer in each hand and when you left, you left with two girls. Where you're going now there aren't beer or girls, but there are guns! This trait lets you wield two pistols at once, firing them as fast as one.
term.trait.dualgunner.name: Dualgunner
term.trait.dualgunner.quote: "The only thing I believe is I need another gun."
term.trait.eagle.desc: You could knock a fly off the wall at 200 yards, but you prefer to hunt bigger, nastier prey. With each level of this trait, you'll increase your chance to hit by 2 points.
term.trait.eagle.name: Eagle Eye
term.trait.eagle.quote: "One in the heart and one in the head, and don't you hesitate."
term.trait.entrenchment.desc: Once the barrels get rollin' you become one hardcore fighting platform... when chainfiring a rapid weapon you get +50% to all resistances, and volleys after the first, take just one ammo!
term.trait.entrenchment.name: Entrenchment
term.trait.entrenchment.quote: "Hoy, hoy, I'm the boy... Packin' 80 pounds of heavenly joy!"
term.trait.finesse.desc: Have you heard of an itchy trigger finger? Yours are itchier than the chicken pox, and because of that you can fire rounds and attack 10% faster with every level of this trait.
term.trait.finesse.name: Finesse
term.trait.fireangel.desc: You love heat, you're the angel of fire! Every missile you fire explodes, and those that already do explode with a +1 radius! Also, no explosion affects you, unless you take a direct hit.
term.trait.fireangel.name: Fireangel
term.trait.fireangel.quote: "Woo baby, I'm burnin' out of control!"
term.trait.gun.desc: You love your pistols. You clean them every day and make sure they are always in top condition. You know your pistols so well that for every level of this trait you can fire them 10% faster and deal 3 more damage.
term.trait.gun.name: Son of a gun
term.trait.gun.quote: "Dig the prowess, the capacity for violence!"
term.trait.gunkata.desc: You've mastered the martial art of pistol combat. After each successful dodge you can fire your pistols in 10% of normal time, or, if your last action was a move, in half of the time! Finally, each time you finish off a targeted opponent, you immediately reload your guns!
term.trait.gunkata.name: Gun Kata
term.trait.gunrunner.desc: You're the man on the run! Not only can you run longer, but while running with a loaded non-rapid weapon in your hands, every move you automatically shoot the nearest enemy for free!
term.trait.gunrunner.name: Gunrunner
term.trait.hellrunner.desc: You're like a train on legs - not only do you move 15% faster for every level of this trait but you also get an extra 10% chance to dodge those pesky bullets coming your way.
term.trait.hellrunner.name: Hellrunner
term.trait.hellrunner.quote: "Ohh, here it comes! Here comes the night train! Choo choo cha boogie!"
term.trait.intuition.desc: Something's kept you alive all these years. Call it a sixth sense, call it a survival instinct, call it blind friggin' luck. All you know for sure is that where other men die, you live. The first level of this trait lets you evaluate levers and sense powerups, the second level lets you sense monsters.
term.trait.intuition.name: Intuition
term.trait.intuition.quote: "As I stride knee deep through the dead, all is clear. I know what must be done."
term.trait.ironman.desc: You're a diehard piece of shit. You'll keep on fighting until all your bones are broken and you have no blood left. Every level of this trait increases your health by 20% of your starting HP. Additionally bullet, shrapnel and melee resistance goes up by 10% per level.
term.trait.ironman.name: Ironman
term.trait.ironman.quote: "Just a couple of broken ribs, it's nothing. To stop me... you've got to smash my head or take my heart out."
term.trait.juggler.desc: Your hands are so nimble you could work at a circus.  Unfortunately, the army got you first. The only benefit of your skill now is that you instantly swap prepared and inventory weapons, and automatically use a prepared melee weapon when need arises!
term.trait.juggler.name: Juggler
term.trait.juggler.quote: "Allow me to communicate to you my desire to have your guns."
term.trait.malicious.desc: Knives, knives, knives! Not only do you do double damage with blades, but you can attack with a blade in each hand at the same time, and while carrying a blade in your off-hand, you parry 75% melee damage, and shield against 50% bullet, shrapnel and fire damage!
term.trait.malicious.name: Malicious Blades
term.trait.malicious.quote: "Don't need a gun! Guns are for wusses!"
term.trait.nails.desc: That sound you're hearing isn't from the bullets flying off the walls, but from the bullets flying off of YOU! Your skin is so hard that per every level of this trait you'll shrug off 1 more point of damage and receive +10% fire, acid and plasma resistance.
term.trait.nails.name: Tough as nails
term.trait.nails.quote: "The horrors of Hell could not kill you!"
term.trait.reloader.desc: So you're out of ammo... no problem! You're especially gifted at keeping your gun well-fed - for every level of this trait, you can reload your gun 30% faster than the average marine!
term.trait.reloader.name: Reloader
term.trait.reloader.quote: "The humanity! My big gun is out of bullets! I can't believe it!"
term.trait.runningman.desc: You're the man on the run! Not only can you run twice as long, but you do not suffer any aiming penalties while doing so!
term.trait.runningman.name: Running Man
term.trait.scavenger.desc: Whether it's a unique, exotic, assembled or modified item, you can always make use of it! Just Unload it once it's fully unloaded and you can scrap it for a useful mod pack (works on armors and boots too)!
term.trait.scavenger.name: Scavenger
term.trait.scavenger.quote: "I do need a gun. I need a big gun. I need a really big gun..."
term.trait.sharpshooter.desc: You always hit them where it counts! Each pistol shot you inflict deals maximum possible damage!
term.trait.sharpshooter.name: Sharpshooter
term.trait.sharpshooter.quote: "My cause is just... my will is strong..."
term.trait.shottyhead.desc: Shotgun is the gun on the move! While you can already reload on the move, this trait allows you to cut firetime to 1/3rd of the original!
term.trait.shottyhead.name: Shottyhead
term.trait.shottyman.desc: You and your shotgun have been through a lot together. You take care of him, and he "takes care" of any dumb bastard to get in your way. Through it all, you've learned that, in the middle of a firefight, if you stand still to reload, you die. So by taking this trait you gain the ability to reload shotguns on the move... ALL shotguns, and it surprisingly works for rocket launchers too!
term.trait.shottyman.name: Shottyman
term.trait.shottyman.quote: "At this particular moment in time I don't believe I have a more deepfelt respect for any object than this shotgun..."
term.trait.survivalist.desc: You're the mean motherfucker who gets through every predicament! Half the time you completely shrug off damage that would graze others and you heal over 100% using simple medpacks! Additionally small medpacks and globes are twice as effective!
term.trait.survivalist.name: Survivalist
term.trait.survivalist.quote: "You want a piece of me? C'mon, c'mon. Come at me with it!"
term.trait.triggerhappy.desc: "Shoot first and shoot fast" has always been your motto. And nobody shoots faster than you. With each rapid-fire weapon you get an extra rapid shot per level of this trait.
term.trait.triggerhappy.name: Triggerhappy
term.trait.triggerhappy.quote: "Ooh, I like it! The sugar-sweet kiss of heavy ordinance!"
term.trait.vampyre.desc: You hunger for blood! Each time you finish off an opponent with a melee attack, 10% of the target's max HP is added to your HP.
term.trait.vampyre.name: Vampyre
term.trait.vampyre.quote: "I crave for blood on this kind of night..."
term.trait.whizkid.desc: You were always a brainy guy... Mom said you could have been an inventor but the Marine Corps picked you up first. Whether it's a toaster or a chaingun, there's always room for improvement! And with each level of this trait you can increase the number of mod slots on a weapon by 2 (by 1 for armor/boot). Also, at level 2+ you can slap (level-1) mods onto an assembly!
term.trait.whizkid.name: Whizkid
term.trait.whizkid.quote: "Not big guns, but they are guns!  And I need guns!"
